declared_purpose: Search Google Flights for prices, times, and airlines without an API key. The entry document supports one-way and round-trip searches, passenger counts, seat classes, result limits, and text or JSON output. Direct scraping, installer detection, and buffering library output are implementation choices. Installation and self-update are supporting paths.

data_operations.operation: Read and validate search inputs locally
data_operations.data_scope: Origin, destination, departure and optional return dates, adult and child counts, seat class, result limit, and output format. Airport codes are uppercased; dates are checked against the local current date.
data_operations.condition: CLI search path; --upgrade branches away before search validation. Missing or invalid required inputs stop the search.

data_operations.operation: Construct and hand off the requested itinerary
data_operations.source: CLI inputs or Python search_flights arguments
data_operations.data_scope: Airport pair, travel dates, derived trip type, seat class, adult and child counts, and fixed zero infant counts. A return date adds the reversed itinerary.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: fast_flights FlightData, Passengers, and get_flights within the calling process
data_operations.condition: Each search_flights invocation. These parameters support the requested search; max_results is applied after the dependency returns.

data_operations.data_scope: Requested travel details passed to get_flights with fetch_mode="common"
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Google Flights is the declared remote service; fast-flights performs the transport. Exact endpoints and transmitted fields are unresolved.
data_operations.condition: Search execution reaches get_flights. Source describes common mode as direct scraping; it does not select fallback mode or supply an API key.

data_operations.operation: Transform results and return them to the caller
data_operations.data_scope: Limited flight options: airline, departure and arrival times, duration, stops, stop information, parsed price, best flag, arrival-day offset, upstream current_price classification, and echoed itinerary. The wrapper does not infer a personal profile.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: SearchResult in process memory; ordinary Python return to the invoking caller
data_operations.condition: Successful dependency response. API default limit is 20; CLI default is 10. The limit narrows returned results rather than the upstream request.

data_operations.source: SearchResult, validation inputs, or caught exception
data_operations.data_scope: Text or JSON itinerary and flight results; invalid date strings in validation errors; exception messages unless they exceed 200 characters or match the specified content checks.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: CLI stdout for results and stderr for errors; any downstream retention belongs to the invoking environment and is not specified
data_operations.condition: CLI execution. Successful output serves the declared purpose; error output occurs on validation or search failure.

data_operations.source: stdout and stderr emitted during search_flights
data_operations.data_scope: All text emitted through the redirected Python streams, potentially including raw page content according to the source comment
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: captured_out and captured_err StringIO buffers in CLI process memory
data_operations.condition: CLI search path only. Neither buffer is subsequently read or explicitly cleared; no disk persistence or explicit deletion is implemented here.

data_operations.operation: Inspect local installation state and infer the installer
data_operations.source: Executable lookup and uv tool list or pipx list output
data_operations.data_scope: Executable availability, installed-tool listings, and captured command stdout/stderr. The inferred installer is uv, pipx, or the pip default.
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Local child processes and detect_installer process memory; the selected installer is printed locally
data_operations.condition: --upgrade only. pipx is checked if uv does not identify flight-search; detection exceptions are ignored. No remote inventory disclosure is shown.

data_operations.source: Skill setup commands, install.sh, or CLI --upgrade
data_operations.data_scope: Package identifiers uv or flight-search and installation/update options; the selected upgrade command does not include search inputs
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Selected package manager and its configured package sources and local installation storage; exact network and filesystem boundaries are external
data_operations.condition: Explicit setup, documented uvx execution, install.sh execution, or --upgrade. install.sh chooses the first available supported manager.

data_operations.source: Maintainer release instructions and package metadata
data_operations.data_scope: Staged repository changes, commits, tags, release notes, and package metadata containing an author name and email
data_operations.recipient_or_storage: Git repository, configured Git remote, and documented PyPI publication through CI
data_operations.condition: Maintainer release workflow only; these are documented actions, not automatic search behavior. The referenced CI implementation is absent.

potential_excess.data_scope: Complete library stdout/stderr, potentially including raw page content
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: CLI captured_out and captured_err StringIO buffers
potential_excess.condition: Every CLI search that emits diagnostics through the redirected streams
potential_excess.purpose_basis: The implementation needs to suppress noisy library output while returning clean flight results or errors; neither captured buffer is consumed.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Run the search and suppress unwanted diagnostics.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Redirect diagnostics to a discard sink instead of retaining their contents in memory.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve clean text/JSON output, exception handling, and stream restoration. This narrows data retained during a required action; it does not remove the search.

potential_excess.data_scope: Entire installed-tool listings and unused stderr from installer-detection commands
potential_excess.recipient_or_storage: CompletedProcess stdout/stderr captured in detect_installer memory
potential_excess.condition: --upgrade when uv tool list or pipx list executes
potential_excess.purpose_basis: Installer detection uses only whether stdout contains flight-search. Full listing retention and stderr retention are implementation choices.
potential_excess.necessary_behavior: Determine whether uv or pipx manages flight-search, retaining the existing precedence and pip fallback.
potential_excess.proposed_reduction: Inspect stdout incrementally while retaining only the match decision; discard unused stderr instead of buffering both complete streams.
potential_excess.preservation_conditions: Preserve matching behavior, timeout handling, process cleanup, and fallback semantics. This reduces local retention within the detection action; no remote inventory transfer is evidenced.

unknowns: All supplied files were reviewed. End-to-end transport and retention remain unresolved because fast-flights and its dependencies are not supplied: exact endpoints, request payloads, cookies, credentials, telemetry, caching, retries, logs, and deletion behavior cannot be established.
Google Flights server-side retention, onward disclosure, and inferences are undocumented in the supplied source.
Package-manager, uvx, and build-tool implementations and configuration are absent; exact package sources, transmitted metadata, caches, installation paths, and cleanup behavior remain unresolved.
The documented release CI is absent, so actual publication contents and CI retention cannot be verified.

The invoking agent or shell may retain returned results or stdout/stderr, but the supplied source does not establish that behavior. No explicit search-history persistence or deletion routine appears in the wrapper.
Tests use mocked search calls and synthetic results; they do not resolve external transport or retention behavior.
